title: A finite ring map is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to T$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $T$, viewed as an $R$-module via $\varphi$, is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $R\to T$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $R\to T$ is quasi-finite at every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PM (lemma-quasi-finite, line 30265), direction 'fibres finite implies quasi-finite', via Lemma Tag 0H8X (lemma-quasi-finite-above-p, line 30245, (2) implies (1)); applied to a finite ring map, whose fibre rings $T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are finite $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras; as used in the proof of Lemma Tag 00QA (lemma-quasi-finite-open, line 30891).
